protocol_amendment.reason: The exact-commit V17 theory and accounting reviews issued scoped GO, but red team issued REVISE before launch-plan design. It found no mathematical change, accounting defect, canonical budget widening, generated-row route, run route, or cryptanalytic overclaim. It found that CLI Path coercion erased terminal output syntax before the direct-Python grammar, the review manifest omitted six normative repository documents and four historical development artifacts, zero-artifact wording did not distinguish current V17/canonical artifacts from historical V1 evidence, arbitrary __fspath__ callbacks could act before admission, and the path-name receipt did not pin Git mode, type, raw path encoding, or control-character handling.

reviewed_v17_root.theory_verdict: GO for separate launch-plan design only

changes: Accept only the V18 document schema and reject V1-V17 without row verification.
Retain verifier and producer CLI --output values as exact Python-decoded strings rather than constructing pathlib.Path during argument parsing.
Require verifier main to apply raw output admission before input verification and pass the same decoded string to the writer.
Control terminal slash and terminal dot spellings through both CLI parsers; require verifier main to reject them before input verification, writing, or parent creation.
Limit raw-spelling claims to the Python-decoded string; raw argv bytes and shell or OS decoding remain external.

State that arbitrary caller __fspath__ code runs before return-value validation and may create caller effects; limit the verifier-created no-destination guarantee to the interval after os.fspath returns and to inert inputs.
Exercise one string-valued callback that creates a caller marker before successful admission and one byte-valued callback that creates its own candidate before exact-type rejection.
Create review-surface-manifest-v18.json with exact repository paths, exact one-level directory selectors, a recursive static experiment selector, and four exact historical-development paths.
Add README, coordinator, executor, idea-generator, task-lifecycle, evidence-and-reproducibility, and shared research-record definitions to the normative review surface.
Reject selected non-ASCII or ASCII-control-bearing paths, require regular nonexecutable mode-100644 blob entries, and hash sorted NUL-delimited mode, type, and raw path records.

Qualify all active authority statements as zero generated V18 curve-family density rows and zero canonical runs while preserving 17 historical V1 development rows and one historical development run manifest.
Preserve the exact V17 implementation, reviews, provenance, and REVISE decision in required and durable inventories.
Retain the completed provenance and predicate vector: 480 prime candidates, 112 draws, 336 curve hashes, 218 point enumerations, and 4218 predicate hashes.
Keep every generated V18 curve-family density-row and canonical-run budget at zero.
unchanged_mathematical_boundary: The curve grid, predicates, four null replicates, representative compiler, ordering digest, graph object, cap schedule, five-field objective, matched-null thresholds, positive gate, and negative classification remain unchanged.
Exactness remains finite, TOY-EVIDENCE, and MODEL-BOUND to the fixed compiler and order-ideal construction.
The standalone complete five-field semantic oracle remains frozen-B4 only; transient B6 and B8 legacy controls reproduce predecessor values but are not independent five-field oracles.
No relation generation, rank, linear algebra, target descent, fixed-curve preprocessing crossover, rho comparison, exponent, deployment, or ECDLP result is in scope.

review_surface_binding.binding_root: fresh reviewer verification of the exact Git commit and tree containing the manifest

residual_external_resource_boundary: Python argument parsing receives decoded strings. V18 does not classify raw argv bytes or prove shell and operating-system decoding behavior.
Calling os.fspath may execute arbitrary same-process caller code before validation. Caller-created side effects are not verifier-created effects and are outside the no-destination theorem.

Exact-attempt reconciliation covers ordinary synchronous Exception subclasses under available memory. KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, process termination, power loss, memory exhaustion, and hostile same-process monkeypatching are not converted into success returns.
An unkeyed receipt detects accidental state confusion but is not authentication against a hostile same-user filesystem actor. Data and receipt snapshots are sequential rather than pair-atomic.

A complete matching receipt is a logical content commit, not proof that every fsync succeeded. Structured publication warnings must be preserved by any future runner, and an immutable external artifact store remains a runner obligation.
Three-or-more leading separators collapse to the ordinary root anchor only on the controlled POSIX runtime; portability outside that runtime is not claimed.
The hard-link and forced ENOTSUP controls establish branch behavior and state transitions, not compatibility or durability of the mounted filesystem.
The one-buffer snapshot and lexical preflight are not CPU, wall-time, peak-RSS, parser-object, allocator-retention, disk, I/O, cache-traffic, or memory-bandwidth guarantees.
Canonical B6 and B8 feasibility, serialized output size, cache occupancy, and role resource use remain unmeasured.

The module-load verifier digest is diagnostic only; a future runner must bind the exact commit, command, environment, immutable paths, hard process limits, publication result, and external resource receipts.
